title: From creek settlement to civic memory
description: The story begins with the fort as a point of protection, exchange, and daily life beside the creek. Archival imagery frames Dubai before the skyline, placing the visitor inside the earliest urban memory of the museum.

title: Walls, towers, wind and shade
description: The architecture scene studies the fort as a working structure: compact defensive geometry, tactile surfaces, shaded rooms, and local construction logic shaped by climate and movement.

title: A timeline mapped through objects
description: Objects become markers in time. Scroll movement connects trade, ceremony, conservation, and interpretation through a guided timeline rather than a static wall of dates.

title: Gallery of living heritage
description: The final scene opens into a gallery rhythm using the prototype imagery: circular masks, wide photographic cuts, and layered images that move at different speeds as the tour continues.
